title: Lake Eyasi: Landscapes and Cultures South of Ngorongoro
excerpt: South of the Ngorongoro highlands lies Lake Eyasi, a quiet soda lake with onion fields, palm groves and the communities of the Hadzabe and Datoga.
body:
Lake Eyasi is a long, shallow soda lake on the southwestern side of the Ngorongoro highlands. It is far from the busy safari routes and feels very different.

## Landscape

A dry, golden landscape with doum palms, acacias and the lake, which shrinks dramatically in the dry season. Flamingos and pelicans can be seen at times.

## Communities

The area is home to several communities, including:

- **Hadzabe**, one of the last hunter-gatherer communities in East Africa.
- **Datoga**, pastoralists known for their metalwork.
- Farmers growing onions with irrigation from the springs.

Visiting the Hadzabe is a sensitive subject; read [visiting the Hadzabe: what to consider](/blog/hadzabe-visit-ethics/).

## Why go

- A cultural experience beyond the parks.
- Quiet, beautiful nature.
- A logical extra night between Ngorongoro and the Serengeti or on the way back.

## Practical

About 1.5 to 2 hours from Karatu, partly on gravel roads.

Read our [Lake Eyasi page](/national-parks/lake-eyasi/) or [plan your trip](/travel-proposal/).
